propositions.text: The claimant is a 27-year-old Mexican citizen claiming refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1)(b).
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXXX, a Mexican citizen, aged 27, is claiming refugee protection in Canada under section 96 and paragraph 97(1)(b) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The claimant is a 27-year-old Mexican citizen claiming refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1)(b), stated by the court.

propositions.text: His life is in danger in Mexico due to threats from his former chief, the drug group 'Gran familia', and federal police.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX XXXXX stated that his life is in danger in Mexico because his former chief, XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX, delegate of XXXXXXXXXXXXXX of the state of XXXXXXX, and his accomplices, the drug trafficking group "Gran familia," as well as the federal police, wanted to kill him.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges his life is in danger from his former chief, drug traffickers, and federal police in Mexico.

propositions.text: His problems began after discovering and reporting his former chief's relationship with the 'Gran familia' cartel.
propositions.quote: His problems began after he realized that his former chief, Mr. XXXXXXXX, had a relationship with the "Gran familia" cartel, and especially after he reported it.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges his problems started after he discovered and reported his chief's cartel ties.

propositions.text: He entered police training in 2007 and began working that same year.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that he entered the police training institute on XXXXX, 2007, and that he began working in XXXXX 2007.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant states he entered police training and began working in 2007.

propositions.text: In 2009, he was mandated to investigate a building in Guanajuato following anonymous reports.
propositions.quote: On XXXXXXX, 2009, following anonymous reports, the claimant was mandated by XXXXXXXXXXXXX to investigate the goings-on in a building located in the XXXXXXX of the city of XXXXXXX, in Guanajuato.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant was mandated in 2009 to investigate a building in Guanajuato after anonymous reports.

propositions.text: The investigation found drug traffickers from 'Gran familia' and seized cellphones linked to federal police officers.
propositions.quote: The investigation revealed that the people who were entering the building were drug traffickers from "Gran familia," and that the investigators had discovered drugs there and had seized cellphones-many of the telephone numbers of these phones were registered to federal police officers, including someone by the name of XXXXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant's investigation found drug traffickers and cellphones linked to federal police officers.

propositions.text: He called one seized cellphone number; his chief answered and questioned how he got the number.
propositions.quote: The claimant called one of these numbers and his chief, XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX, answered and asked him how he had obtained his private number.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant called a seized number; his chief answered and questioned him.

propositions.text: He said he got the number from the public ministry office, but his chief said no one there knew it.
propositions.quote: The claimant responded that he had obtained it from the office of the public ministry because he had asked for it urgently, but his chief told him that no one at the public ministry knew this number.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant said he got the number from the public ministry, but his chief denied anyone there knew it.

propositions.text: Despite this, he reported finding his chief's cellphone number among the traffickers' phones.
propositions.quote: Despite everything, the claimant wrote in his report that he had found his chief's cellphone number in the drug traffickers' cellphones.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant reported his chief's cellphone number was found among traffickers' phones.

propositions.text: In 2005, his chief ordered him to stop the investigation and destroy evidence, threatening problems if he did not comply.
propositions.quote: On XXXX, 2005, the claimant was summoned by his chief, Mr. XXXXXXXX, who ordered him to stop the investigation and to destroy all of the evidence that he had accumulated, and he added that if he did not do it, he would have problems.

paragraphs.summary: In 2005, his chief ordered him to stop investigating and destroy evidence, threatening him.

propositions.text: He refused, found his investigation file missing, reported his chief and accomplices to the coordinator, and gave him the only copy of his investigation.
propositions.quote: The claimant refused to obey his chief and, on XXXXXXX, 2009, he realized that his investigation file had disappeared. The next day, he made an appointment with the coordinator of the ministerial police station, XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX, and reported his chief, XXXXXXXXXXXX, and his federal police accomplices, as well as the "Gran familia" cartel. He alleged that he gave the only copy of his investigation to the coordinator, after telling him that his report and the proof found had disappeared.

paragraphs.summary: He refused orders, found his file missing, reported his chief and accomplices, and gave the coordinator his only investigation copy.

propositions.text: The coordinator advised him to leave things as they were; he then received a threatening call.
propositions.quote: The coordinator advised him to leave things as they were and, on XXXXX, 2009, the claimant received a threatening telephone call on his cellphone.

paragraphs.summary: The coordinator advised inaction; the applicant then received a threatening call.

propositions.text: He went again to the area coordinator, who insulted and beat him, telling him he had many enemies.
propositions.quote: Once again, he went to the area coordinator, Mr. XXXXXX, who told him that he had many enemies, insulted him and beat him.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant was insulted and beaten by the area coordinator, who said he had many enemies.

propositions.text: He requested protection from the Office of the Attorney General, but was told no physical protection was available.
propositions.quote: The claimant requested protection from the Office of the Attorney General, before the chief of the area's public ministry, who told him that he could not offer him any physical protection.

paragraphs.summary: He sought protection but was told no physical protection could be offered.

propositions.text: His verbal threats were not registered as an offence; he was physically assaulted and reported it with a medical certificate but was not given a complaint copy.
propositions.quote: On XXXX, 2009, he went to the public ministry of XXXXXXX, where the officer did not register his report in a preliminary special investigation report because they were verbal threats and they did not constitute an offence unless physical assault was involved. That same day, four individuals in a pickup truck threatened him with a weapon and beat him. The claimant went to the clinic and then to the public ministry, where he reported the physical assault and submitted a medical certificate. He clarified, however, that he was not given a copy of the complaint.

paragraphs.summary: Verbal threats were not registered; he was physically assaulted, reported it, but was not given a complaint copy.

propositions.text: His chiefs summoned him and an agent of harm and asked for his resignation.
propositions.quote: On XXXXXX, 2009, his chiefs summoned him and the agent of harm and asked for his resignation.

paragraphs.summary: His chiefs asked him and the agent of harm to resign.

propositions.text: Three masked men came to his home; he escaped and applied for a passport.
propositions.quote: On XXXXX, 2009, three masked men went to his home but he managed to get away from the house and went to XXXXXX. He applied for his passport on XXXXX, 2009.

paragraphs.summary: Three masked men came to his home; he escaped and applied for a passport.

propositions.text: Four men tried to intercept him getting into a taxi; he escaped and was told to limit his complaint to that incident.
propositions.quote: On XXXX, 2009, four men tried to intercept him as he was getting into a taxi. Once again, he was able to escape and went to the public ministry, where he was told to limit his complaint to the incident that had occurred that same day.

paragraphs.summary: Four men tried to intercept him; he escaped and was told to limit his complaint to that incident.

propositions.text: He took refuge in the state of Mexico, was victim of attempted kidnapping, escaped, then went to the public ministry and Puebla.
propositions.quote: The claimant took refuge in XXXXXXX, in the state of Mexico, but on XXXX, 2009, he was the victim of an attempted kidnapping by two people, and once again, he was able to get away. He returned to the public ministry and then went to Puebla.

paragraphs.summary: He took refuge, was kidnapped but escaped, then went to the public ministry and Puebla.

propositions.text: He decided to leave Mexico and arrived in Canada on June 21, 2009.
propositions.quote: On XXXX, he decided to leave Mexico and arrived in Canada on June 21, 2009.

paragraphs.summary: He left Mexico and arrived in Canada on June 21, 2009.

propositions.text: The claimant's identity was satisfactorily established by his passport seized by Citizenship and Immigration Canada.
propositions.quote: The claimant's identity was established satisfactorily by means of his passport, which was seized by Citizenship and Immigration Canada (CIC).

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant's identity was satisfactorily established by his passport seized by CIC.

propositions.text: The claimant's testimony had many implausibilities and omissions undermining his credibility.
propositions.quote: The claimant's testimony contained numerous implausibilities and some omissions that undermined his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant's testimony contained many implausibilities and omissions undermining credibility.

propositions.text: The claimant testified he discovered a superior's ties to drug traffickers and included this in a report that later disappeared.
propositions.quote: He testified that, in an investigation, he discovered that XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX XXXXXX had connections with the drug traffickers of the "Gran familia" group and that, after he discovered this, he included this information in a report that disappeared from his office afterward.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified he found a superior's drug ties and made a report that disappeared.

propositions.text: The claimant said XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX was superior to his team chief, and he worked in a team of XX police officers.
propositions.quote: When asked to explain whether XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX was his immediate superior, the claimant responded that he was the superior of his team chief, XXXXXXXXXX. When he was asked to explain whether he was alone on that investigation, the claimant responded that they were a team of XX police officers.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX was superior to his team chief and he worked in a team of XX officers.

propositions.text: The claimant testified he checked cellphone numbers seized and encountered XXXXXXX XXXXX who questioned how he got his private number.
propositions.quote: The claimant also testified that, when he wanted to check who the telephone numbers belonged to on the cellphones seized in the drug traffickers' home, he came across XXXXXXX XXXXX, who allegedly asked him how he had obtained his private number.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified he checked seized cellphone numbers and was questioned about his private number.

propositions.text: It is surprising the claimant checked numbers without informing his chief; his excuse about how he got the private number is unrealistic and implausible.
propositions.quote: The panel considers it surprising that the claimant, who worked on a team of 15 people and who had a group chief, had taken the initiative to check the numbers seized without informing his chief. The excuse that the claimant allegedly gave to the XXXXXXX about how he had found his private number is completely unrealistic and implausible.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds it surprising the claimant checked numbers without informing his chief and his excuse is implausible.

propositions.text: If obtaining the private number was necessary, it likely would be the group chief's task, not the claimant's.
propositions.quote: In fact, if a situation came up in which the XXXXXXX's private number absolutely needed to be obtained, it is likely that this would be the task of the group chief, who, according to the hierarchy, is between XXXXXXXXXXX and the claimant.

propositions.text: It is surprising the group chief did not order the number check or hold the report and evidence that disappeared.
propositions.quote: It is also surprising that the order to check the numbers found was not given by the group chief and that the report and the evidence, which according to the claimant were stolen from his office, were not requested and held by the group chief.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds it likely the group chief should have obtained the number and is surprised he did not order the check or hold the missing report.

propositions.text: The claimant testified that after discovering drug ties, XXXXXX asked him to stop the investigation but he refused.
propositions.quote: The claimant also testified at the hearing that, after he discovered the ties between the drug traffickers and XXXXXXXXXXX, the XXXXXXX asked him to stop the investigation and the claimant refused to do so.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified XXXXXX asked him to stop the investigation but he refused.

propositions.text: It is implausible that XXXXXXXXXXXX contacted the claimant to stop the investigation instead of asking the group chief.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that it is implausible that XXXXXXXXXXXX contacted the claimant to tell him to stop the investigation, when he could have simply asked the group chief, Mr. XXXXXX, to stop the investigation, since he was his hierarchical superior.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds it implausible that XXXXXXXXXXXX contacted the claimant to stop the investigation instead of the group chief.

propositions.text: Since XXXXXXXXXXX was superior, it is surprising he did not tell drug traffickers to destroy evidence if tied to them.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, since XXXXXXXXXXX was XXXXXXXXXXXXXX superior, he could not ignore that there was an investigation under way into the building, and it is, at the very least, surprising that if he was tied to the drug trafficking group, he did not tell them to make the evidence disappear.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds it surprising that XXXXXXXXXXX did not tell traffickers to destroy evidence if tied to them.

propositions.text: The claimant testified the searched home belonged to drug traffickers; he had an arrest warrant and conducted about ten inspections.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the claimant testified that the home that was allegedly searched belonged to the drug traffickers of the "Gran familia" group; when asked whether the home was guarded and to specify how he entered, the claimant responded that they had an arrest warrant. He then specified that he had carried out about ten inspections of the home and that he had checked each of the cellphones found and, when he called XXXXXXXXXXX, he told him that he was calling to give him the results of the inspection.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified the searched home belonged to traffickers; he had an arrest warrant and did about ten inspections.

propositions.text: The explanation that the claimant called XXXXXXXXXXX on a private number to give an inspection report is not valid.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that this explanation is not valid because there is no reason why the claimant, who had received the mandate from XXXXXXXXXXXX, would call XXXXXXXXXXX on a private number, claiming that he wanted to give him an inspection report.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant's explanation for calling XXXXXXXXXXX on a private number to give a report is invalid.

propositions.text: The claimant said XXXXXXXXXXXX was surprised when told he asked for his number to update on the investigation.
propositions.quote: Confronted with that implausibility and asked to explain how XXXXXXXXXXXX had reacted when he responded, the claimant stated, [translation] "He was surprised; I told him that I had asked for his number to fill him in on the investigation."

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said XXXXXXXXXXXX was surprised when told he asked for his number to update on the investigation.

propositions.text: The claimant testified he wrote and kept an investigation report at the archives office; colleagues knew but had no copies.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the claimant testified that he wrote an investigation report and that he kept it; he specified that the report was kept at the archives office. He also testified that his colleagues knew about the report but did not have a copy of it because they were busy with other investigations.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified he wrote and kept an investigation report at archives; colleagues knew but had no copies.

propositions.text: The claimant testified he submitted a copy of the report to XXXXXXXXXXX but not to his group chief; the copy disappeared after demand.
propositions.quote: The claimant also testified that he had submitted a copy of the report, after XXXXXXX, to XXXXXXXXXXX, but that he had not given a copy to his group chief, XXXXXXXXXXX. He testified that XXXXXXXXXXXX demanded that he give him the report and that his copy then disappeared.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified he gave a report copy to XXXXXXXXXXX but not to his chief; the copy disappeared after demand.

propositions.text: The claimant did not know why he omitted giving the report to XXXXXXXXXXXX in his Personal Information Form.
propositions.quote: When asked to explain why he did not indicate in his Personal Information Form (PIF) that he gave the report to XXXXXXXXXXXX, the claimant responded that he did not know.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant did not know why he omitted giving the report to XXXXXXXXXXXX in his Personal Information Form.

propositions.text: The omission about the report is significant and undermines credibility; the panel doubts the incident occurred.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that it is a significant omission that undermines the claimant's credibility in that it concerns an incident that is central to the refugee protection claim. In addition, the claimant's testimony about the procedure to follow for producing and archiving investigation reports was not clear or specific, and the panel does not believe that such an incident ever occurred.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the omission about the report significant, undermining credibility, and doubts the incident occurred.

propositions.text: The claimant testified chiefs asked him to resign; he was attacked, followed, and is a threat to powerful enemies.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that the chiefs asked him to resign and that he was a victim of several attacks and attempted killings. He also specified that he was followed and found in XXXXX and in XXXXX. When asked why his powerful enemies, that is, Police XXXXXXXXXXXX, the members of the "Gran Familia" cartel, and other police officers of the federal investigations agency (AFI) would continue to look for him everywhere, the claimant responded that he is a threat to them.

propositions.text: The claimant did not demonstrate his enemies have reasons to feel threatened by him; his report disappeared and complaints failed.
propositions.quote: The claimant did not demonstrate that his powerful enemies have reasons to feel threatened by eventually being reported by him; the report and the evidence allegedly disappeared and all of his attempts to file complaints were to no avail.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified he was attacked and is a threat to enemies, but did not show enemies had reason to fear him; report disappeared and complaints failed.

propositions.text: The panel does not believe the claimant's story is true.
propositions.quote: The panel does not believe that this story is true.

paragraphs.summary: The court does not believe the claimant's story is true.

propositions.text: The claimant did not prove a serious possibility of persecution or risk of torture, death, or cruel treatment if returned to Mexico.
propositions.quote: After analyzing the testimonial and documentary evidence, the panel concludes that the claimant did not discharge his burden of establishing that there is a "serious possibility" that he would be persecuted on one of the Convention grounds. He did not demonstrate, on a balance of probabilities, that should he return to Mexico, he would be personally subjected to a danger of torture or to a risk to his life or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the claimant failed to prove a serious possibility of persecution or risk if returned to Mexico.

propositions.text: The panel determines that the claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: the panel determines that the claimant is not a "Convention refugee" or a "person in need of protection."

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes the claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.

propositions.text: The panel rejects the refugee protection claim of the claimant.
propositions.quote: The panel rejects the refugee protection claim of XXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects the claimant's refugee protection claim.
